Search is changing quickly.


Customers still use Google to find local businesses, but they’re also asking AI-powered tools for recommendations, comparing options inside AI-generated answers, and using conversational search to find what they need.


That creates a new visibility challenge for small businesses.


You might rank well in traditional search and still have little visibility when a customer asks ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, or another AI search experience to recommend a business.


That’s where[Answer Engine Optimization](https://www.thryv.com/blog/answer-engine-optimization-shorten-customer-decision-journey/) , or AEO, comes in.


AEO services help make your business easier for search engines and AI systems to understand, evaluate, and potentially surface in answers. For local businesses, that work usually starts with the same fundamentals that support strong SEO: accurate business information, helpful website content, positive reviews, structured data, and a consistent presence across the web.


The challenge is figuring out which provider can actually help.


There are plenty of agencies now offering AEO, GEO, AI search optimization, and related services. Some focus heavily on technical SEO. Others specialize in content, digital PR, AI visibility tracking, or enterprise brands.


So, which options make sense for a small business?


We’ve compared nine AEO service providers using criteria that matter to local service businesses, including trades, health and wellness, beauty, professional services, and other businesses that rely on customers finding them online.

## **What Are AEO Services?**


AEO services are professional services designed to improve how easily search engines and AI-powered answer engines understand and potentially surface a business, its content, and its expertise.


Traditional SEO focuses primarily on helping webpages rank in search results. AEO expands that work to answer-focused experiences, including AI-generated answers, conversational search, voice search, featured snippets, and other zero-click experiences.


The two strategies overlap significantly.


AEO can include:


- Answer-first website content
- Question-based content strategy
- Structured data and schema markup
- Google Business Profile optimization
- Local listings management
- Review and reputation management
- Entity and brand optimization
- Digital PR and authority building
- AI visibility monitoring
- Content optimization
- Technical SEO
- Reporting and performance measurement


In other words,[AEO isn’t about stuffing more keywords into your website](https://www.thryv.com/blog/small-business-seo-mistakes-to-leave-behind/) .


It’s about making your business information clear, useful, trustworthy, and easy for search systems to interpret.


That’s particularly important for local businesses.


If someone asks, “Who is the best plumber near me?” or “What are the best family law firms in Seattle?” an[AI system needs enough reliable information](https://www.thryv.com/blog/what-is-ai-search/) to understand which businesses exist, what they offer, where they operate, and whether customers trust them.


Your website is one piece of that picture. Your listings, reviews, social profiles, third-party mentions, and other online signals can also contribute to how your business is understood.


The[2026 BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/) reports that 45% of consumers used AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity to find a local business during the past year, compared with 6% the year before.


The takeaway is simple: **getting found online increasingly means being visible beyond traditional search results.**


##
**What Should AEO Services Include?**


The best AEO services don’t just promise to “get you into ChatGPT.”


They should address the underlying information and authority signals that help search engines and AI systems understand your business.


Here are the capabilities worth looking for.


### **1. Answer-first website content**


Your website should clearly answer the questions customers ask before they contact you.


That could include:


- What services do you offer?
- How much does the service cost?
- Where do you provide service?
- How quickly can customers get help?
- What should customers know before hiring you?
- What makes your business different?
- What questions should customers ask before choosing a provider?


Good[AEO optimization services](https://www.thryv.com/boosts/search-engine-optimization/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) structure this information so both people and search systems can quickly find the answer.

### **2. Structured data and schema**


[Schema markup](https://www.thryv.com/blog/schema-markup-for-small-businesses-aeo-guide/) gives search engines additional context about the information on your website.


Depending on the page and business, this can include structured information about your organization, services, locations, products, FAQs, and other relevant content.


Schema isn’t a magic button for appearing in AI answers. But when used appropriately, it can help search systems interpret your content more clearly.


### **3. Accurate business listings**


Local businesses need consistent information across the web.


Your business name, address, phone number, website, hours, services, and service areas should be accurate and consistent across important platforms.


That matters for traditional local search and can also strengthen the overall picture search systems have of your business.


See our guide to[local search](https://www.thryv.com/blog/local-search/) for more ways to improve local visibility.


### **4. Google Business Profile optimization**


Your[Google Business Profile](https://www.thryv.com/features/local-listings/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) is one of the most important pieces of a local search strategy.


An AEO provider should understand how your profile connects with your website, listings, reviews, services, and broader local presence.


### **5. Review generation and reputation signals**


Reviews do more than influence whether someone calls your business.


They also provide context about customer experiences, services, locations, and areas of expertise.


An effective visibility strategy should include a plan for[generating authentic reviews](https://www.thryv.com/features/automated-reviews/%20?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) and maintaining a strong online reputation.


### **6. Content that answers real customer questions**


AEO isn’t about publishing hundreds of generic AI-generated articles.


It is about[creating useful content that answers questions](https://www.thryv.com/features/ai-for-small-businesses/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial#ai-content-assistant) your customers actually ask.


For example, a roofing company could create content around:


- How long does a roof replacement take?
- How much does a roof replacement cost?
- Does homeowners insurance cover roof damage?
- How often should a roof be inspected?


The goal is to demonstrate expertise while making information easier to find and understand.


### **7. AI visibility monitoring**


Some AEO providers monitor how often a business or brand appears in AI-generated answers.


That can include tracking mentions, citations, competitors, prompts, platforms, and changes over time.


Keep expectations realistic, though.


AI-generated answers can vary by query, location, user context, model, and time. No legitimate provider can guarantee that your business will appear in ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Perplexity, or another AI platform.


### **8. Reporting tied to business outcomes**


Visibility is useful, but visibility alone isn’t the goal.


Your provider should explain how[AEO work connects to meaningful outcomes](https://www.thryv.com/features/ai-for-small-businesses/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial#ai-leads) such as:


- Organic traffic
- Calls
- Form submissions
- Quote requests
- Bookings
- Leads
- Conversion rates
- AI referral traffic
- Search visibility
- Local rankings


That makes it easier to determine whether your investment is actually helping your business grow.


## **What to Look for in a Provider**


We evaluated providers using the same criteria throughout this list and looked at what matters when a small business is deciding whether an AEO investment makes sense.


### **Our evaluation criteria**


**Best fit:** Who is the provider designed to serve?


**Local-business relevance:** Does the provider support local, service-area, or multi-location businesses?


**AEO scope:** Does the offering cover content, schema, listings, reviews, AI visibility, technical optimization, or related services?


**SEO foundation:** Does the provider connect AEO with traditional SEO?


**Reporting:** Does the provider explain how performance is measured?


**What to verify:** Are pricing, deliverables, contracts, ownership, and AI visibility claims clear?


Because AEO is still an evolving category, pricing and deliverables can change quickly. Always confirm current pricing, scope, contract terms, and platform coverage before signing an agreement.


For small businesses, it’s also worth remembering that AEO should generally build on your existing SEO foundation rather than replace it. That’s consistent with the brief’s recommendation and with the way leading providers position AEO today.

## **AEO vs. SEO Services: How They Work Together for Local Visibility**


AEO and SEO aren’t competing strategies.


SEO helps your business become visible in traditional search. AEO helps make your business and content easier for AI-powered systems to understand and potentially surface in answers.


For most small businesses, you need both.


**** **SEO** **AEO**


**Primary goal** Improve visibility in traditional search Improve visibility in AI-generated answers


**Where it appears** Search results, maps, local packs AI answers, AI Overviews, conversational and voice search


**Key focus** Keywords, content, technical SEO, links, local signals Clear answers, context, entities, schema, authority and citations


**Content approach** Match search intent and provide helpful information Provide clear, concise answers to specific questions


**Local visibility** Maps, local results, location-based searches AI recommendations and answers about local businesses


**Measurement** Rankings, traffic, calls, leads, conversions Mentions, citations, AI visibility, referral traffic and business outcomes


Think of[SEO as the foundation](https://www.thryv.com/blog/seo-vs-aeo-vs-geo-why-its-all-still-seo/) and AEO as an extension of that foundation.


The same things that help customers and search engines understand your business can also help AI systems interpret your business.


That’s why AEO shouldn’t mean abandoning the fundamentals.


Your business still needs:


- A useful website
- Accurate listings
- Strong local SEO
- Relevant content
- Positive reviews
- Quality backlinks
- Consistent business information
- A technically healthy website


## **How to Pick an AEO Provider That Fits Your Business**


You don’t necessarily need the biggest AEO agency.


You need the provider that solves your biggest visibility problem.


Start with these four steps.


### **1. Check your current visibility**


Before paying for AEO services, find out how your business currently appears.


Search for:


- Your business name
- Your primary services
- Your services plus your city
- “Best \[service\] near me”
- “\[service\] in \[city\]”
- Common questions your customers ask


Then see what happens when you ask AI tools similar questions.


Are you appearing?


Are competitors appearing instead?


Is the information about your business accurate?


Are your services and location represented correctly?


A visibility audit can help answer these questions before you commit to an ongoing service.


### **2. Identify your biggest gap**


Your problem might not actually be AEO.


You may need:


- Better local listings
- More customer reviews
- Better service pages
- Stronger backlinks
- A faster website
- More useful content
- Better Google Business Profile optimization
- More consistent business information


Fixing the foundation may deliver more value than immediately investing in a specialized AEO program.


### **3. Decide how much work you want to manage**


Some providers are strategic consultants.


Others handle content and implementation.


Some offer full-service marketing.


And some tools allow you to manage much of the work yourself.


Be honest about how much time you have.


If you’re already running a plumbing company, dental practice, salon, law firm, HVAC business, or other local operation, you probably don’t want another marketing platform that requires hours of weekly management.


A[done-for-you service](https://www.thryv.com/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) may be worth the investment if it saves your team time and keeps your strategy moving.


### **4. Compare at least two or three providers**


Ask every provider the same questions:


- What exactly is included?
- Which AI platforms do you monitor?
- Do you handle content?
- Do you implement schema?
- Do you manage local listings?
- Do you support Google Business Profile optimization?
- Do you help generate reviews?
- Do you build backlinks?
- How do you measure AI visibility?
- How do you connect visibility to leads?
- Who owns the content and accounts?
- Is there a long-term contract?
- What happens if I cancel?
- What results should I reasonably expect in the first 3, 6, and 12 months?


Most importantly, pay attention to how the provider talks about results.


Expert Tip


No AEO company can guarantee that your business will appear in ChatGPT or another AI platform.


AI-generated answers can change based on the question, location, context, platform, model updates, and information available to the system.


A credible provider should talk about improving the signals within its control rather than promising a guaranteed AI citation.

1. Connects AEO with traditional SEO.


1. Addresses your website and local search foundation.


1. Provides clear deliverables.


1. Measures visibility over time.


1. Explains how success connects to business outcomes.


1. Makes realistic claims about AI visibility.


1. Is transparent about pricing, contracts, ownership, and ongoing work.


The right AEO provider should make your business easier to understand, not just sell you another marketing buzzword.
